pattern.summary: 8 questions, attempt any 5, each carries 20 marks. Mostly theory with many 'compare' and 'short notes' questions; a few questions on ratios, NPV/IRR and depreciation.

choosing: Cyber security (CIA principles, authentication vs authorisation, CAPTCHA, GDPR) appears in every paper — the most reliable topic.
'Compare' and 'short notes' questions (4–5 parts × 4–5 marks) reward broad revision: learn one-line differences for every pair in the Key points.
Mail merge, operating systems and e-payment methods are asked most sessions.
numerical: For ratios, write the formula, then an example with figures, then what a high or low value means.
For NPV/IRR, show the Excel syntax: =NPV(rate, value1, …) + initial outlay, and =IRR(values).

topics.name: Cyber Security, Authentication & Data Protection
topics.summary: CIA principles, authentication vs authorisation, 2FA and OTP, CAPTCHA, identity theft, firewall, GDPR vs DPD.
points: Cyber security: protecting systems, networks and data from attacks.
Principles (CIA triad): Confidentiality (only authorised access), Integrity (data not altered), Availability (accessible when needed); also authentication and non-repudiation.
Authentication verifies who you are (password, OTP, fingerprint); authorisation decides what you may access.
Two-factor authentication: two different factors (something you know + something you have/are), e.g. password + OTP. OTP: a one-time code sent by SMS/app, valid briefly.
Access control policy: rules for who can access what (role-based access, least privilege).
Penetration testing: authorised simulated attack to find weaknesses.
Firewall: hardware/software that filters traffic between a trusted and an untrusted network.
Identity theft: stealing personal data (Aadhaar, card details) to commit fraud.
CAPTCHA: test that tells humans from bots — text, image, audio, math, reCAPTCHA; protects forms and logins.
GDPR (EU, 2018) replaced DPD (1995): a regulation (binding directly) vs a directive; wider scope, consent rules, right to be forgotten, breach notification in 72 hours, heavy fines.
Public key encrypts, private key decrypts (asymmetric encryption); digital signatures use the private key.
topics.frame: Definition → principles with one example each → a comparison table where asked → conclusion.

topics.name: Software & Operating Systems
topics.summary: System vs application software, OS functions and types, language processors, utility programs, open source.
points: System software runs the computer (OS, drivers, utilities); application software does user tasks (Word, Tally).
Operating system: manages hardware and provides services to programs. Functions: process, memory, file, device and security management, user interface.
Types: batch, time-sharing, real-time, distributed, network, mobile (Android, iOS), desktop (Windows, Linux).
Android (open source, Linux-based, mobile) vs Windows (proprietary, desktop).
Language processors: compiler (translates whole program at once, faster execution), interpreter (line by line, easier debugging), assembler (assembly to machine code).
Utility programs: antivirus, disk cleanup, backup, compression, disk defragmenter.
Free and open-source software: source code available to use, modify and share (Linux, LibreOffice).
File management: organising and storing files; memory management: allocating RAM to processes.
topics.frame: Definition → functions or types as headed points → comparison table → examples.

topics.name: Networks, Internet & E-mail
topics.summary: Network types, internet vs intranet vs extranet, WWW, URLs and domains, browsers, e-mail protocols, cloud computing.
points: Computer network: connected devices sharing data and resources.
Types by area: PAN (personal), LAN (building), MAN (city), WAN (country/world), HAN (home).
Internet (public, global), intranet (private, within an organisation), extranet (intranet opened to partners).
WWW is a service on the internet (web pages linked by hyperlinks); the internet is the network itself.
URL: web address — protocol://domain/path. Domain types: gTLD (.com, .org) and ccTLD (.in, .uk).
E-mail protocols: SMTP sends; POP3 downloads and usually deletes from server; IMAP syncs and keeps mail on the server.
Cloud computing: using storage and software over the internet (Google Drive, OneDrive); models IaaS, PaaS, SaaS.
Graphical browsers (Chrome) show images; non-graphical (Lynx) show text only.
topics.frame: Definition → types in a table (range, example) → comparisons → conclusion.

topics.name: MS Word, PowerPoint & Google Docs
topics.summary: Mail merge, word processing features, equation editor, presentations and animation, Google Docs vs Word.
points: Mail merge: creates personalised letters, labels or envelopes from one main document and a data source.
Components: main document, data source (list of recipients), merge fields; steps: prepare document → connect data source → insert fields → preview → finish and merge.
Word processing: creating, editing, formatting and printing text documents; features include indenting, styles, tables, spell-check, bookmarks, track changes, equation editor.
Bookmark: a named location in a document you can jump to.
PowerPoint views: Normal, Slide Sorter, Reading, Slide Show; insert charts via Insert → Chart, diagrams via SmartArt.
Steps to prepare a presentation: purpose and audience → outline → design/theme → content and visuals → animation and transitions → rehearse.
Google Docs: free, online, real-time collaboration, auto-save, version history; Word is richer offline but collaboration needs OneDrive.
topics.frame: Meaning → steps as a numbered list with menu paths → uses in business → conclusion.

topics.name: Ratios, Capital Budgeting & Depreciation
topics.summary: Ratio analysis, NPV and IRR (with Excel syntax), depreciation methods, loan and lease statements, payroll.
points: Ratio analysis: comparing figures from financial statements to judge liquidity, profitability and efficiency.
Current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities (ideal 2:1). Quick ratio = (current assets − inventory − prepaid) ÷ current liabilities (ideal 1:1).

Gross profit ratio = GP ÷ net sales × 100; net profit ratio = NP ÷ net sales × 100; operating cost ratio = (COGS + operating expenses) ÷ net sales × 100; inventory turnover = COGS ÷ average inventory.
Capital budgeting: evaluating long-term investment projects. Methods: payback, ARR, NPV, IRR, profitability index.
NPV = present value of inflows − initial outlay; accept if NPV > 0. IRR: discount rate at which NPV = 0; accept if IRR > cost of capital.
Excel: =NPV(rate, cash flows) + initial outlay (negative); =IRR(range including the outlay).
Depreciation: straight line (same amount each year) vs diminishing balance (fixed % on reducing balance); Excel =SLN(), =DB().
Loan statement: principal, interest, EMI schedule (=PMT()); lease statement: lease rentals for using an asset without owning it.
Payroll: calculation of salaries, allowances and deductions (PF, tax) for employees.
mistakes: Forgetting that Excel's NPV() does not include the year-0 outlay.

topics.name: E-payment, Plastic Money & Wallets
topics.summary: E-payment methods, plastic money, NEFT vs RTGS, digital wallets, QR codes, B2B vs B2C.
points: E-payment: paying electronically instead of cash or cheque. Methods: debit/credit cards, net banking, UPI, e-wallets, NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, QR codes.
Plastic money: debit, credit, prepaid and smart cards; grew with banking reach, POS terminals, safety and convenience.
NEFT: batch-wise settlement, no minimum amount. RTGS: real-time, one by one, minimum ₹2 lakh — for large payments.
Digital wallet: stores money for quick payments (Paytm, PhonePe); success helped by demonetisation, UPI and smartphones.
QR code: a 2-D barcode storing encoded information (e.g. UPI ID) that a phone can scan and decode.
Precautions: never share OTP/PIN, use secure sites (https), check merchant details, enable alerts.
B2B: business sells to business (IndiaMART); B2C: business sells to consumers (Amazon).
topics.frame: Meaning → methods as headed points → merits and precautions → conclusion.

topics.name: Business Information Systems (MIS, DSS, ERP)
topics.summary: Business and information systems, MIS vs DSS, ERP, data vs information, business ownership forms.
points: Data: raw facts; information: processed, meaningful data.
Business information system: people, hardware, software, data and procedures that support business operations and decisions.

Types: TPS (transactions), MIS (routine reports for middle managers), DSS (what-if analysis for semi-structured decisions), EIS (top management), ERP (integrates all departments on one database — SAP, Oracle).
MIS vs DSS: structured, periodic reports vs interactive, ad-hoc analysis.
Business by ownership: sole proprietorship (one owner, unlimited liability), partnership (2+ partners, agreement), company (separate legal entity), co-operative.
topics.frame: Definition → block diagram (inputs → processing → outputs, with feedback) → types → importance for business.

topics.name: DBMS, RDBMS & Data Models
topics.summary: File processing vs DBMS, DBMS vs RDBMS, data models, data abstraction and independence, database administrator.
points: File processing limits: redundancy, inconsistency, difficult access, isolation, integrity and security problems.
DBMS: software to store, retrieve and manage data centrally (MS Access, MySQL).
RDBMS stores data in related tables with keys and SQL (Oracle, MySQL); DBMS may store data as files without relations.
Data models: hierarchical (tree), network (graph), relational (tables), entity-relationship, object-oriented.
Data abstraction: three levels — physical (how stored), logical (what is stored), view (what a user sees).
Data independence: changing one level without affecting the next (physical and logical independence).
DBA: designs the schema, grants access, handles backup and recovery, tunes performance.
topics.frame: Definition → diagram of the three levels → comparison table → conclusion.

topics.name: Computer Fundamentals & Generations
topics.summary: What a computer is, generations, types (analog/digital/hybrid, micro to super), hardware components, applications.
points: Computer: a programmable electronic device that accepts data (input), processes it and gives results (output), and stores them.
Hardware: input devices, CPU (ALU, CU, registers), memory (RAM, ROM), storage, output devices. Software: system and application.
Generations: 1st vacuum tubes; 2nd transistors; 3rd integrated circuits; 4th microprocessors; 5th AI and parallel processing; 6th (emerging) quantum and nano computing.
By data: analog (continuous), digital (discrete), hybrid (both). By size: micro, mini, mainframe, super.
Mainframe: many users, large transaction processing (banks). Supercomputer: fastest, scientific calculations (weather).
Applications: business, banking, medicine (diagnosis, records, imaging), defence (simulation, communication), education.
topics.frame: Definition with a block diagram (Input → CPU → Output, with memory) → classification table → applications.

topics.name: YouTube, AdSense & Digitisation
topics.summary: YouTube channels and revenue, Google AdSense, digitisation's impact on business, AI.
points: YouTube: video platform for marketing, training and brand building.
Create a channel: sign in with a Google account → Create a channel → name, logo, description → upload videos → customise.
Revenue: YouTube Partner Programme (1,000 subscribers and 4,000 watch hours) and AdSense for ads; challenging due to competition and eligibility rules.
Google AdSense: places ads on websites and YouTube and pays publishers per click or view. Advantages: free, easy, trusted advertisers. Limitations: strict policies, low earnings without traffic.
Digitisation: converting information and processes to digital form — faster service, lower cost, online markets, data-driven decisions.
Google Play Store: Android's app store.
topics.frame: Meaning → steps or advantages as headed points → examples → conclusion.

topics.name: DPR, Research Proposal & Data Analysis
topics.summary: Detailed project report, research proposal components, data collection, frequency distribution, correlation and regression.
points: DPR (detailed project report): the final plan used for funding and approval. Components: executive summary, promoters, market analysis, technical details, cost of project, means of finance, profitability, risks.
Research proposal: title, introduction, problem statement, objectives, literature review, hypothesis, methodology, time frame, budget, references.
Data collection: primary (survey, observation, interview) and secondary (published sources).
Frequency distribution table: shows how often each value or class occurs.
Correlation measures the strength of relationship; regression predicts one variable from another.
topics.frame: Meaning → components as a numbered list → conclusion.

topics.name: MS Excel Features & Functions
topics.summary: Charts, worksheets, relative vs absolute addressing, logical and financial functions, formulas vs functions.
points: Relative reference (A1) changes when copied; absolute ($A$1) stays fixed; mixed ($A1).
Formula: user-written expression (=A1+B1). Function: built-in formula (=SUM(A1:A10)). Array formula works on a range at once.
Logical functions: IF, AND, OR, NOT, IFERROR. Financial functions: PMT, FV, PV, NPV, IRR, SLN, DB.
Charts: select data → Insert → chart type; organise with chart titles, legends, axes, move to a new sheet.
Worksheets: insert, delete, rename, move, group (select several with Ctrl) and ungroup.
Cell comments/notes explain entries; Track Changes records edits in shared workbooks.
topics.frame: Meaning → syntax with an example formula → use in business → conclusion.
